title: Design an ETA / Delivery-Time Prediction System
prompt: Design a system that predicts estimated time of arrival for rides or deliveries. Given an origin, destination, and current conditions, it must return an accurate ETA within tight latency, using spatiotemporal features (traffic, road network, historical patterns) and a model that stays accurate as conditions change through the day.
blurb: Spatiotemporal ML at scale: routing + traffic features, low-latency regression serving, real-time conditions, and drift across time-of-day/weather.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (predict ETA, update en route, per-segment vs end-to-end, uncertainty) from non-functional (low-latency serving, accuracy targets, availability, freshness of traffic).

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about request volume, latency budget, accuracy metric/target, coverage regions, how ETA is used (pricing, dispatch, UX), en-route re-estimation.

rubric.label: Back-of-envelope estimations
rubric.description: Derives QPS, latency budget, feature fetch cost, model inference cost, storage for trips/traffic history, GPS/telemetry ingest rate.

rubric.label: Spatiotemporal feature pipeline
rubric.description: Road-graph/route features, real-time traffic (speeds per segment), historical time-of-day/day-of-week patterns, weather/events, geohash/segment aggregation, freshness.

rubric.label: Model & low-latency serving
rubric.description: Route-based vs learned end-to-end model, segment-level prediction + aggregation vs holistic, feature fetch + inference path, batching, timeout/fallback.

rubric.label: Training-serving parity
rubric.description: Same feature computation offline/online, point-in-time-correct traffic snapshots (no future leakage), logging served features, backtesting on historical conditions.

rubric.label: Feedback & labels
rubric.description: Actual trip durations as labels, censored/incomplete trips, per-segment ground truth from GPS traces, retraining cadence, seasonality.

rubric.label: Evaluation & drift
rubric.description: Regression metrics (MAE/MAPE, quantile/pinball loss, calibration of uncertainty), sliced by region/time-of-day, drift from traffic-pattern shifts, weather, events.

rubric.label: High-level design
rubric.description: Request → routing/candidate path → feature fetch (real-time traffic + historical + context) → model → ETA + uncertainty; async telemetry stream updating traffic features and labels.

rubric.label: Scaling & reliability
rubric.description: Horizontal serving, geo-sharded feature store, caching per segment/route, graceful fallback (historical baseline) when real-time features stale, regional deploys.

rubric.label: Observability
rubric.description: Latency SLOs, prediction error tracking vs actuals, feature freshness (traffic staleness), calibration monitoring, drift alerts by region/time.

rubric.label: Privacy & integrity
rubric.description: GPS/location privacy, anonymization/aggregation of traces, preventing manipulation of ETA for pricing/dispatch abuse.

functional_requirements: Predict ETA for an origin→destination request
Re-estimate en route as position and conditions change
Return an uncertainty/quantile, not just a point estimate
Incorporate real-time traffic and historical patterns
Serve ETA to dispatch, pricing, and rider/eater UX
nonfunctional_requirements: Low-latency serving (p99 ~50-100ms) for interactive UX and dispatch
Accuracy targets (e.g. MAPE / on-time rate) by region
High availability with a historical-baseline fallback
Fresh traffic features (segment speeds updated in seconds/minutes)
Reproducible predictions with logged features + model version
clarifying_questions: Latency budget, and is ETA on the interactive path or async?
What accuracy metric and target matter to the business?
How is ETA consumed — pricing, dispatch matching, UX, SLAs?
Do we predict end-to-end, or per-segment then aggregate?
Do we re-estimate continuously en route?
qualifying_questions: Ride-hailing (point-to-point) or multi-stop delivery with prep time?
Dense urban with rich traffic data or sparse regions?
Is a physics/routing engine already available, or learn from scratch?

estimations.traffic: ~10K ETA requests/sec peak plus continuous en-route re-estimates → effective QPS much higher
estimations.latency_budget: ~80ms p99 = routing/candidate path + feature fetch (segment speeds) + inference + aggregation
estimations.telemetry: Millions of active devices emitting GPS every few seconds → high-throughput ingest feeding real-time segment-speed aggregation
estimations.storage: Trip history + per-segment speed time series: many TB; retain 13+ months for seasonality; hot store for recent traffic
estimations.model: GBM or spatiotemporal NN; segment-level + route aggregation; CPU inference feasible, GPU if deep sequence model

core_components: Real-time traffic aggregation (segment speeds from telemetry)
data_model: trips(trip_id PK, origin, dest, route, predicted_eta, actual_duration, model_version, ts)
segment_speeds(segment_id, geohash, speed, updated_at) — real-time online store
segment_history(segment_id, tod_bucket, dow, historical_speed) — offline patterns
api_design: internal: completed-trip actuals joined to predictions for labels
reference.high_level_design: A request resolves a route over the road graph (or candidate paths), then fetches features: real-time per-segment speeds from an online store fed by GPS telemetry, historical time-of-day/day-of-week speed patterns from an offline store, and context (weather, events). The model predicts either per-segment travel times aggregated over the route or an end-to-end duration, returning a point ETA plus quantiles for uncertainty. En route, the system re-estimates using current position and updated traffic. Telemetry streams continuously into a real-time aggregation job that maintains fresh segment speeds; completed trips produce actual durations that join to predictions as labels. A training pipeline retrains on historical trips with point-in-time-correct traffic snapshots, backtests across time-of-day/weather regimes, and rolls out via shadow + A/B, while a drift monitor watches error by region and time bucket. If real-time traffic features are stale or the model is unavailable, the system falls back to a historical-baseline ETA.

deep_dives.probe: Do you predict per-segment travel times and sum them, or learn one end-to-end model? What are the accuracy, latency, and en-route-update tradeoffs?
How do you turn millions of GPS pings into fresh per-segment speeds at low latency? Handle sparse segments, outliers, and freshness.
When you train on historical trips, how do you reconstruct the traffic state as it was at prediction time — point-in-time snapshots — so you don't leak future traffic into training?
Dispatch and SLAs care about being late, not just the mean. How do you predict and calibrate uncertainty (quantiles), and why is that better than a point ETA?
Traffic patterns shift with time-of-day, weather, events, and seasonality. How do you detect drift and decide when to retrain, and how do you evaluate sliced by region/time?
Real-time segment speeds go stale or the model server is down. What ETA do you return, and how does the historical baseline work?

The road network and segment attributes (closures, new roads, speed limits) change in a source map system. How do those changes propagate into the routing graph and feature store so ETAs aren't computed on a stale map?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions feature store or segment or traffic features
followup_bank.question: When the road network or segment attributes change in the source map DB (closures, new roads), how does the routing graph and feature store stay in sync — CDC/change-stream driven update, or scheduled rebuild? What staleness do you tolerate?
You cache segment speeds or route ETAs — what's the eviction/TTL, and when traffic or the map changes how do you invalidate stale-after-change entries so you don't serve an outdated ETA?
How do you roll out a new ETA model — shadow scoring against actuals, A/B, and rollback on which error metric?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions telemetry or GPS or streaming
followup_bank.question: How do you handle late/out-of-order or sparse GPS data in your real-time segment-speed aggregation, and what freshness do you guarantee?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions MAE or MAPE or accuracy or error
followup_bank.question: Why slice error by region and time-of-day, and how do you monitor calibration of your uncertainty estimates?
How is the historical-baseline fallback computed, and when exactly do you switch to it?

scaling: Geo-sharded feature store keyed by segment/geohash
Horizontally scaled stateless serving with route/segment caches
Partitioned real-time traffic aggregation by geo region
Regional model deployments; historical baseline as always-available fallback
Batch precompute of common routes / popular OD pairs
bottlenecks: Real-time traffic aggregation lag hurting freshness
Feature fetch for long multi-segment routes
tradeoffs: Segment-level (flexible, en-route updates) vs end-to-end (simpler, sometimes more accurate)
Richer spatiotemporal model vs inference budget
Point estimate (simple) vs quantiles (better decisions, more complexity)
alternative_solutions: Pure routing-engine ETA with speed profiles (no ML) as baseline/fallback
Graph neural network over the road network for spatial correlation
Sequence models over the route for en-route updates
Hybrid: physics/routing prior + ML residual correction
observability: Live prediction error vs actuals (MAE/MAPE) sliced by region/time
Drift alerts on error by segment/region/time bucket
security: Location/GPS privacy — aggregate and anonymize traces
Access control on telemetry and trip data
Prevent ETA manipulation that games pricing/dispatch
Rate limiting and anti-scraping on the ETA API
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer builds a spatiotemporal pipeline: resolve a route on the road graph, fetch fresh per-segment speeds (from streaming GPS telemetry) plus historical time-of-day/day-of-week patterns and context, and predict either per-segment times aggregated over the route or end-to-end — returning calibrated quantiles, not just a mean, because dispatch/SLAs care about lateness. It enforces training-serving parity with point-in-time-correct traffic snapshots so training never leaks future traffic, logs served features, and backtests across time/weather regimes. It uses completed-trip actuals as labels, retrains on a seasonality-aware cadence, and evaluates MAE/MAPE/pinball sliced by region and time-of-day. It keeps traffic and the road graph fresh via a change-driven update pipeline, degrades to a historical baseline when real-time features are stale or the model is down, and monitors error and drift by region/time as a first-class concern.

interviewer_notes: Steer the candidate to treat this as a spatiotemporal data problem, not a generic regression. Early, get them to decide segment-level vs end-to-end prediction and to justify it against en-route updates. The senior separators: (1) training-serving skew via point-in-time-correct traffic snapshots — push hard, because reconstructing 'traffic as it was at prediction time' is where leakage hides; and (2) uncertainty/quantiles + sliced evaluation — a point ETA and a single MAPE number is a mid-level answer; strong candidates predict calibrated quantiles and slice error by region/time-of-day. When they place a feature store or routing graph, hit the CDC/freshness probe about how map/road-network changes propagate. When they add a segment-speed or route cache, probe eviction and stale-after-change invalidation. Always force the fallback answer: what ETA is returned when real-time traffic is stale or the model is down. Reserve time for drift across time-of-day/weather/seasonality and safe model rollout against actuals.
